From 13a9d08c296228d18289de60b83792c586e1d073 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Aug 2022 18:00:30 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] net: lan966x: improve error handle in
 lan966x_fdma_rx_get_frame()

Don't just print a warning.  Clean up and return an error as well.

Fixes: c8349639324a ("net: lan966x: Add FDMA functionality")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Horatiu Vultur <horatiu.vultur@microchip.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/YwjgDm/SVd5c1tQU@kili
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c
index 6dea7f8c1481..51f8a0816377 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c
@@ -425,7 +425,8 @@ static struct sk_buff *lan966x_fdma_rx_get_frame(struct lan966x_rx *rx)
 	lan966x_ifh_get_src_port(skb->data, &src_port);
 	lan966x_ifh_get_timestamp(skb->data, &timestamp);
 
-	WARN_ON(src_port >= lan966x->num_phys_ports);
+	if (WARN_ON(src_port >= lan966x->num_phys_ports))
+		goto free_skb;
 
 	skb->dev = lan966x->ports[src_port]->dev;
 	skb_pull(skb, IFH_LEN * sizeof(u32));
@@ -449,6 +450,8 @@ static struct sk_buff *lan966x_fdma_rx_get_frame(struct lan966x_rx *rx)
 
 	return skb;
 
+free_skb:
+	kfree_skb(skb);
 unmap_page:
 	dma_unmap_page(lan966x->dev, (dma_addr_t)db->dataptr,
 		       FDMA_DCB_STATUS_BLOCKL(db->status),
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c`**
1. **Line Modification**: The original line that used `WARN_ON` to check if `src_port` is greater than or equal to `lan966x->num_phys_ports` has been modified. Instead of just issuing a warning, it now checks the condition and, if true, jumps to the `free_skb` label to handle the error.
2. **Error Handling**: A new label `free_skb` has been added, which calls `kfree_skb(skb)` to free the socket buffer (`skb`) before exiting the function. This ensures that memory is properly cleaned up in case of an error.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification enhances the error handling mechanism in the `lan966x_fdma_rx_get_frame` function. Previously, the function would only print a warning if the `src_port` was invalid, potentially leading to memory leaks if the function exited without freeing the allocated `skb`. The new implementation not only warns about the invalid `src_port` but also ensures that the allocated resources are cleaned up by freeing the `skb` before returning an error. This change improves the robustness of the code by preventing resource leaks and ensuring proper error handling.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
WARN_ON(src_port >= lan966x->num_phys_ports);
```
```c
skb = build_skb(page_address(page), PAGE_SIZE << rx->page_order);
```
```c
if (unlikely(!skb))
    goto unmap_page;
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the `WARN_ON` statement only issues a warning when `src_port` is invalid (i.e., greater than or equal to `num_phys_ports`), but it does not handle the cleanup of the allocated socket buffer (`skb`). If `skb` is successfully allocated but `src_port` is invalid, the function can exit without freeing `skb`, leading to a memory leak. Additionally, if `skb` allocation fails, the function jumps to `unmap_page`, which does not handle the case where `src_port` is invalid.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (WARN_ON(src_port >= lan966x->num_phys_ports))
    goto free_skb;
```
```c
free_skb:
    kfree_skb(skb);
```
Reason:
The fix introduces a conditional check that, if `src_port` is invalid, will jump to the `free_skb` label, ensuring that the allocated socket buffer (`skb`) is properly freed before the function exits. This prevents memory leaks by ensuring that any allocated resources are cleaned up in the event of an error condition.
